texts: For a Marfan woman at 32 weeks whose aortic root has grown from 38 to 42 mm, the book's plan is an elective caesarean section at term, followed by aortic root replacement.
Pregnancy raises the risk of dissection in Marfan syndrome, especially when the root is over 40 mm or growing.
A planned caesarean at term spares the aorta the stress of labour and lets the baby reach full maturity; the root is replaced after delivery.
Immediate delivery at 32 weeks exposes the baby to prematurity without a pressing maternal need, and ending the pregnancy is not indicated.
Echo surveillance and beta-blockade continue until delivery.
In the picture, Caesar lifts the baby out on the pumpkin's day, and only then does Franky put the bendy straw in place of the salsa jar.
Memory hook: the ripe pumpkin first, then the bendy straw.
